scope.description: Hand-researched deepening pass for English Fossil and eight rows that show fossil revival, legendary birds, holo/non-holo duplicate rows, and the trainer hinge that gives the set its name.
not_claiming: Japanese Mystery of the Fossils equivalence

sources.title: Local English WoC release catalog: Fossil
Pokemon TCG API v2 set record: Fossil

claims.text: The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API model English Fossil as released on October 10, 1999.
The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API both model Fossil as a 62-card English Wizards of the Coast set.
Bulbapedia describes Fossil as an English expansion corresponding to the Japanese Mystery of the Fossils era, while the local catalog treats the English release as its own release_family_id.

The local Fossil catalog's opening holo rows include Aerodactyl, Articuno, Dragonite, Gengar, Lapras, Moltres, and Zapdos, while Mysterious Fossil appears as the common trainer row that makes the fossil mechanic legible.
The local Fossil artist credits for the promoted rows include Kagemaru Himeno, Mitsuhiro Arita, Keiji Kinebuchi, and Ken Sugimori.

Fossil matters because it turns the early binder into an excavation site: prehistoric Pokemon, legendary birds, ghost-line atmosphere, and the Mysterious Fossil trainer make discovery itself part of the card-game apparatus.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, want, scan, or agent memory says Fossil, English Fossil, Mystery of the Fossils, legendary birds, Fossil Dragonite, Fossil Gengar, or Mysterious Fossil.
special_identification_instructions.summary: English Fossil is a 62-row Wizards release; preserve language, set id, row number, and holo/non-holo distinction.
steps: Preserve release_family_id en_wotc_fossil_19991010 for the English Wizards release.
Do not collapse English Fossil into Japanese Mystery of the Fossils without naming the language and release-family change.
For headline Pokemon with both holo and non-holo rows, preserve the exact card number and rarity signal before treating rows as equivalent.
Do not infer 1st Edition, shadowless, print-error, or condition claims from the catalog row alone.
For fossil-themed identity, separate Pokemon rows from the Mysterious Fossil trainer row that supports evolution in play.
not_claiming: Japanese Mystery of the Fossils equivalence

narrative.why_it_matters: Fossil is one of those early sets that changes the room temperature. Jungle made the world feel alive; Fossil makes it feel buried, haunted, and waiting to be uncovered. The legendary birds give the sky a mythic ceiling, Gengar gives the caves a grin, Dragonite gives the set a soft surprise, and Mysterious Fossil makes the idea of recovery mechanical. It is not just a set of old creatures. It is a lesson in how Pokemon turns absence into play.

sources.title: Pokemon TCG API v2 card record: Aerodactyl

claims.text: The local catalog identifies Fossil row base3-1 as Aerodactyl.
The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API record Aerodactyl base3-1 as Rare Holo.
The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API credit Aerodactyl base3-1 to Kagemaru Himeno.
Aerodactyl matters because it is the set's thesis card: a fossil creature returned as a holo, with the name of the set made visible in one prehistoric silhouette.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing or want says Fossil Aerodactyl, Aerodactyl holo, Aerodactyl 1, or Aerodactyl 16.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Aerodactyl base3-1 is the Rare Holo row; keep it separate from the non-holo rare row base3-16.
steps: Preserve card id base3-1 and Rare Holo rarity when the evidence points to this row.
Compare against base3-16 before treating a generic Fossil Aerodactyl mention as the holo.
Do not infer 1st Edition, print-error, condition, or authenticity from the catalog row alone.
Record Kagemaru Himeno as the catalog illustrator credit, but do not use artist credit alone as physical-card identity.

narrative.human_title: The fossil that wakes the set
narrative.why_it_matters: Aerodactyl is Fossil saying its own name out loud. It is old life turned back into a card, and Himeno's credit gives the prehistoric idea a softer creature presence than the premise might suggest. The row is also a clean agent test: Aerodactyl has both holo and non-holo Fossil rows, so affection has to yield to number.

narrative.human_title: The soft giant in the bone set
narrative.why_it_matters: Dragonite is Fossil's emotional surprise. The set is ancient, sharp, and haunted, then Himeno gives it this rounded, generous creature. That tension is the charm. A collector may chase the holo because it is Dragonite; an agent has to care that it is specifically base3-4, not the non-holo row and not an error claim smuggled in by memory.

It is a chase card because people love Gengar; it is a Fossil card because the whole set feels like something looked back from the dark.

sources.title: Pokemon TCG API v2 card record: Mysterious Fossil

claims.text: The local catalog identifies Fossil row base3-62 as Mysterious Fossil.
The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API record Mysterious Fossil base3-62 as Common.
The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API credit Mysterious Fossil base3-62 to Keiji Kinebuchi.
Mysterious Fossil matters because it turns the set's title into a play object: fossil Pokemon are not only pictured, they are mechanically staged through a Trainer row.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing or want says Mysterious Fossil, Fossil trainer, fossil evolution support, Aerodactyl fossil, Kabuto fossil, or Omanyte fossil.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Mysterious Fossil base3-62 is the common Trainer row that supports fossil evolution context; do not collapse it into a Pokemon species row.
steps: Preserve card id base3-62 and Common Trainer identity.
Do not treat Mysterious Fossil as Aerodactyl, Kabuto, Omanyte, or any other fossil Pokemon row.
When a buyer wants fossil Pokemon support or binder completeness, distinguish Trainer row completion from Pokemon row completion.
Record Keiji Kinebuchi as the catalog illustrator credit, but do not use artist credit alone as physical-card identity.

narrative.human_title: The little hinge under the whole set
narrative.why_it_matters: Mysterious Fossil is humble, but it is the hinge. Without it, Fossil is mostly a theme; with it, the theme becomes a rule. Kinebuchi's trainer row tells the agent that the set's deepest idea is not just old Pokemon. It is the act of bringing something buried into play.
